headline: ASX closed up slightly today while last night's Wall St session saw the NASDAQ drop 2.2% — and the big local story is Labor locking in a CGT and negative gearing deal with the Greens.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a strong session today, jumping 3.47% to $5.66. Lithium stocks got a bounce on renewed optimism around the sector, with analysts flagging PLS as a potential comeback candidate. The company is also ramping up spending on its P2000 expansion project — a big bet on future lithium demand, though some analysts flag execution risk at this stage of the cycle.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft rose 1.8% in last night's session to $373.94, bucking a broadly weak NASDAQ. The catalyst: news that Microsoft has locked in a 20-year power deal with Chevron for a West Texas AI data centre — a strong signal of long-term AI infrastructure commitment that investors liked.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two climbed 1.28% last night to $242.64. GTA VI buzz continues to drive sentiment — a leak suggested an $80 base price for the game, though insiders pushed back on the figure. Regardless, ongoing hype around the title is keeping the stock well-supported.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI.AX rose 1.01% today to $17.97, riding positive AI sector sentiment on the ASX despite a rough night for US tech. The ETF tracks global AI-related companies, so local buyers stepped in while US markets were closed.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 0.77% last night to $346.08. No specific company news drove the move, but sentiment was hurt by reports that Google has lost two top AI researchers — one to OpenAI and one to Anthropic. In a field where talent is everything, losing key researchers to rivals is a real concern.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS.AX nudged up 0.54% today to $527.36. This ETF tracks the entire US sharemarket and tends to reflect the prior night's US session — last night's S&P 500 drop of 1.44% didn't flow through fully, as the ASX opened on a more stable footing today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG.AX edged up 0.22% today to $76.90. As a diversified multi-asset ETF, it held up well. Strong inflows into ASX ETFs broadly are keeping demand healthy for products like this one.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE.AX dipped 0.35% today to $94.67. Emerging markets faced a headwind from the Aussie dollar falling 1.33% against the USD — a weaker AUD can affect how global assets are priced locally, and investor caution around developing economies persisted today.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL.AX fell 0.37% today to $8.13. Oil (WTI crude) dropped 1.65% last night to $72/barrel after analysts downgraded their oil forecasts following the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — a key shipping lane in the Middle East. Macquarie, who had been calling for $200 oil, has now slashed its Brent crude outlook, which weighed on energy stocks globally.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Strong bounce, but still down 16% overall
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals had its best session in a while today (+3.47%), but you're still sitting on a $24 loss overall (-16%). The P2000 expansion is a long-term bet on lithium demand recovering. Worth holding if you believe in the lithium story, but no rush to add more just yet — sentiment can flip quickly in this sector.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Powering ahead on AI infrastructure story
watch_today.detail: Microsoft rose 1.8% last night and locked in a 20-year energy deal with Chevron for AI data centres. That's a serious long-term commitment. MSFT is currently down 15.6% in your portfolio, but the AI tailwind is real and building. Hold — this one looks like it needs time, not an exit.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Talent drain to rivals worth watching
watch_today.detail: Google dropped 0.77% last night and the bigger concern is two senior AI researchers leaving for OpenAI and Anthropic. In AI, people ARE the product pipeline. You're still up 12.6% on GOOG, but keep an eye on whether this becomes a pattern. Hold for now — one story doesn't break the thesis.

watch_today.title: Labor-Greens CGT & negative gearing deal — property investors take note
watch_today.detail: Labor has struck a deal with the Greens to reduce the capital gains tax (CGT) discount — which currently lets property and share investors pay tax on only 50% of their gains — and tighten negative gearing rules on existing properties. If passed, this could affect the after-tax value of selling investments. Worth understanding before your next portfolio decision.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike risk back on the table
watch_today.detail: Australia's inflation data this week showed headline CPI cooling, but the 'core' measure (the underlying rate that strips out volatile items) remains sticky. Bond traders are now not ruling out a fourth rate rise. If the RBA hikes again, that's bad for growth stocks and good for the Aussie dollar — both matter for your portfolio.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Oil forecasts cut after Hormuz reopens
watch_today.detail: The Strait of Hormuz — a critical oil shipping chokepoint between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula — has reopened, easing supply fears. Macquarie, which had been forecasting $200 oil, has dramatically cut its outlook. Wood Mackenzie now sees Brent at US$78/bbl in 2027. Lower oil prices are a headwind for FUEL.AX. Consider whether your energy exposure still fits your view.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 closed up a modest 0.24% today at 8,808 — a relatively calm local session. Last night on Wall Street was a different story: the NASDAQ dropped 2.21% and the S&P 500 fell 1.44%, dragged down by broad tech selling. Oil slid 1.65% to $72/barrel after Middle East supply fears eased. Gold also pulled back 0.91% to $4,092/oz. The Aussie dollar fell 1.33% to US$0.69 — a meaningful drop that makes your US holdings worth slightly less in AUD terms.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Modest gain today — local market held its nerve despite a weak Wall St session overnight.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw a meaningful selloff, led by tech stocks.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech-heavy index took the hardest hit last night — down over 2%.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil dropped as the Strait of Hormuz reopened, easing fears of a supply crunch.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pulled back slightly — still near historically elevated levels.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar fell sharply — makes your US stock holdings worth a little less in AUD today.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is Labor sealing a deal with the Greens on capital gains tax and negative gearing reform — a change that will directly affect property investors and anyone holding shares or assets long-term. Meanwhile, the RBA is dominating financial headlines with inflation data keeping rate hike fears alive.

stories.title: Labor and Greens strike deal on CGT and negative gearing reform
stories.why_it_matters: Labor has done a deal with the Greens to pass changes to capital gains tax (CGT) and negative gearing. The CGT discount — which currently means you only pay tax on 50% of a capital gain when you sell an asset like shares or an investment property — is set to be reduced, making investment profits more expensive come tax time. Negative gearing on existing properties (where you claim rental losses against your income) will also be tightened. This directly affects property investors and long-term share investors. If you're planning to sell any investments, this is worth understanding before the legislation passes.

stories.title: RBA rate hike fears alive as inflation data shows sticky core CPI
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's latest inflation figures show the headline rate is cooling, but 'core' or underlying inflation — the measure the RBA watches most closely — is still running hot. This is keeping traders on alert for another interest rate rise, even after the RBA has already hiked multiple times. Bond traders (the people who bet on where rates are heading) are not ruling out a fourth rate rise this cycle. Higher rates mean more expensive mortgages and tougher conditions for businesses — but they also tend to push the Aussie dollar higher.

stories.title: Bond traders won't rule out fourth RBA rate rise
stories.why_it_matters: AFR is reporting that bond traders — who are essentially the market's most informed rate-watchers — are pricing in a real chance of a fourth RBA rate hike in this cycle. This comes despite headline inflation easing, because the stickier underlying inflation measure hasn't come down fast enough to give the RBA comfort. For mortgage holders, another hike would mean more pain. For investors, higher rates tend to put downward pressure on share valuations, particularly growth stocks.

stories.title: Business groups blast Albanese government's procurement changes
stories.why_it_matters: Business groups are pushing back hard against the Albanese government's changes to how the government buys goods and services (procurement rules). Industry bodies say the changes 'sow the seeds of corruption' by reducing competitive tendering and making it easier for the government to direct contracts to preferred suppliers. This is a developing story about how taxpayer money gets spent — and whether small and mid-sized businesses get a fair shot at government contracts.

ai.summary: The big AI talent story today is Google losing two senior researchers to rivals OpenAI and Anthropic — a real concern for GOOG holders. Elsewhere, ByteDance (TikTok's parent) is targeting a July launch for a new AI video model, Microsoft is deploying AI tools for government policy work, and South Australia is pushing hard to attract AI data centres.

stories.title: Google loses two top AI researchers to OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.why_it_matters: Google has lost two of its top AI researchers — one has jumped to OpenAI and another to Anthropic, two of Google's biggest rivals in the AI race. In an industry where breakthrough ideas come from a handful of elite researchers, this kind of talent drain matters. It adds to the competitive pressure on Google's AI division (DeepMind and Google Brain) and may partly explain why GOOG's stock dipped last night. For GOOG holders, it's worth watching whether this becomes a trend rather than a one-off.

stories.title: ByteDance targeting July launch of upgraded AI video model
stories.why_it_matters: ByteDance — the Chinese company behind TikTok — is planning to launch an upgraded AI video generation model in July. This puts them in direct competition with OpenAI's Sora and Google's Veo in the fast-moving AI video space. The ability to generate realistic video from a text prompt is one of the most commercially valuable AI capabilities right now — think advertising, film, education, social media. ByteDance has significant resources and a massive distribution network through TikTok, making them a serious competitor to watch.

stories.title: Microsoft deploys AI tools to support government policy analysis
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft is expanding its AI business into government and public policy work, publishing details of how its tools are being used to help analyse policy options and build public sector capability. This is a growing market — governments worldwide are starting to use AI to process large amounts of data and model policy outcomes faster. For MSFT holders, government contracts are a high-value, long-duration revenue stream that complements its enterprise cloud business.

stories.title: South Australia pushes for AI data centres as industry says it's not asking for subsidies
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia is actively pitching itself as a home for AI data centres, with the state government in discussions with industry players. The AI industry says it's not asking for direct cash subsidies — rather, it wants streamlined approvals and access to renewable energy infrastructure. Data centres are a huge and growing part of AI infrastructure spend globally, and states that attract them get jobs, tax revenue and energy grid investment. This is part of a broader Australian push to become a regional AI hub.

sport.summary: NRL Round 17 kicks off Thursday night with Eels vs Rabbitohs. There's plenty of transfer activity with the June 30 deadline looming. In AFL, Collingwood is pushing to shake up pre-game traditions and the Liam May situation at Melbourne is escalating. Wimbledon is also underway with a young Aussie making waves.

stories.title: NRL faces mid-season shake-up before June 30 transfer deadline
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL's mid-season transfer window closes June 30 — just days away — and several clubs are expected to make moves. Five players have been identified as likely to find new clubs before the deadline, with teams scrambling to plug injury and form holes heading into the second half of the season. Wests Tigers have already been active, signing a replacement for Jarome Luai. Expect more announcements in the next few days.

stories.title: Perth Bears signings tracker: Building toward the 2027 NRL season
stories.why_it_matters: CODE Sports has published a full rundown of every signing made so far by the Perth Bears — the NRL's 18th team set to debut in 2027. The article includes a projected best 17 based on current signings. With the June 30 deadline approaching, the Bears are in a critical recruitment window as they try to build a competitive squad from scratch for their inaugural season.

stories.title: 'Frightening' Collingwood move behind Liam Neale trade frenzy; Swans make big call on 2027 targets
stories.why_it_matters: Collingwood is reportedly making an aggressive push to sign Brisbane Lions midfielder Liam Neale, which Fox Sports describes as 'frightening' for rival clubs given their salary cap flexibility. Meanwhile, Sydney Swans have made a significant call on their 2027 trade targets. Both stories signal the AFL trade period heating up well before the official window opens, with big clubs positioning early.

stories.title: Joanna Garland: 'My dream is to play Wimbledon one day'
stories.why_it_matters: Young Australian tennis player Joanna Garland has been speaking about her ambitions ahead of Wimbledon, telling the Australian Open website that playing at the All England Club is her dream. Garland is emerging as one of the promising young names in Australian women's tennis, and with Wimbledon underway, she's one to watch in the coming rounds.
